commander_specific_reason: Removing a finality counter is directly tied to the commander's unique drawback and can add a +1/+1 counter to the same creature; repeatability is more valuable than one-shot opponent-graveyard value.
Utility land can relocate finality counters off a commander-reanimated Pirate; replacing a tapped tri-land is a real fixing trade-off, but 34 lands and other UBR sources remain.
Three-mana flying Pirate can temporarily convert one artifact/creature per player into Treasure, creating broad tempo and repeatable ETB value with counter mitigation.

A Pirate that can be reanimated with haste and activated for {2}{U}{U} to take an extra turn once City Blessing is achieved. It trades a reliable draw vehicle for a high-ceiling commander-reanimation target.
Its ETB life loss is immediate when reanimated and Roaming Throne can double the Pirate trigger. It is symmetric and risks your life total; use when the life cushion permits.

Excellent 6/6 trample and combat-damage draw with graveyard-cast permission, but mandatory draw is redundant with the existing draw suite and it is not a Pirate. Navigator provides an extra-turn line from commander reanimation.

Damage doubling is powerful and it is a Pirate, but the seven-mana static payoff is less immediate than Ravager's ETB, which can be doubled by Roaming Throne and reused through finality-counter mitigation.

Navigator costs four mana to activate and needs City Blessing; it is not infinite because it goes to the library bottom. Its Pirate type and extra-turn value when reanimated with haste fit the commander better than a non-Pirate draw engine.

candidate_or_comparison: Dire Fleet Ravager vs Angrath's Marauders
commander_specific_reason: Ravager's ETB affects all players and can be doubled by Roaming Throne; finality-counter removal makes repeated ETB possible. Self-life loss is the primary drawback.
Four-mana artifact with slow tap/sorcery-speed setup; the deck already has commander reanimation, Living Death, Patriarch's Bidding and finality-counter mitigation.
Useful flying Pirate, but its attack/parley value gives opponents cards and overlaps existing Treasure/card-advantage density.
Tapped land and expensive activation are slow; Nesting Grounds directly supports finality-counter reuse without adding a high-cost land activation.
Three-mana mill activation on a colorless land is too slow given Admiral Brass mills four on entry and the list has Entomb, Buried Alive and looting.
Saga can steal from graveyards but is slower and less focused than the current Pirate reanimation engine.
Tribal anthem and draw are strong but five mana and redundant with current draw/tribal engines; high-end slots are better used for Pirate ETB payoffs.
Optional combat draw and force-attacks are useful, but the deck already has Kindred Discovery, Black Market Connections, Malcolm, Francisco and Windfall.
Equipment offers menace, stats and looting but adds equip/attack setup; the deck's commander payoff is better supported by ETB/reanimation pieces.
Repeatable temporary theft is on-theme but costs four mana to cast plus four per activation; Don Andres, Hostage Taker and Larcenist are more efficient.
Seven-mana wipe is expensive and overlaps existing mass-removal/reanimation effects; treasure payoff does not offset the cost.
Flexible but non-Pirate and lower-impact than current graveyard setup and interaction; does not improve the finality engine.
Three-mana anthem plus activation overlaps Skeleton Crew, Corsair Captain and Shared Animosity; it does not add a high-impact reanimation target.
Efficient flying Pirate but its late draw activation is expensive and the deck already has more impactful draw engines.
Looting and Treasure are on-plan, but the tap-based setup overlaps current graveyard/card access and doesn't add a high-impact ETB.
Repeatable unblockability is useful, but the slot is better spent on the finality-counter engine and high-impact reanimation targets.
Instant-speed creature bounce can protect or reset, but it also removes the deck's own Pirate board and overlaps existing reset effects.
Flexible graveyard/artifact/combat answer is good, but no current interaction slot was a better cut than the chosen additions.
Monarch and unblockability can help, but the deck's draw density is sufficient and the slot is better used for repeatable ETB/extra-turn payoff.
Convoke removal is efficient, but the deck already has targeted removal and board wipes; it is not a Pirate or finality-engine piece.
Evasion and team unblockability are useful but four-mana activation is expensive; current evasion is adequate for the reanimation plan.
Strong attacking Pirate anthem, but current combat scaling is sufficient; the deck prioritizes finality-counter reuse and high-impact ETB targets.
Can remove counters for card draw, but it is a 2/2 non-Pirate and costs a tap plus a counter; Power Conduit's counter removal also grows a creature or charges an artifact.
Clone effect is flexible, but it is a higher-cost non-Pirate and does not improve finality-counter mitigation or ETB repeatability as directly.
Useful Pirate first strike and opponent-graveyard value, but Power Conduit makes the commander’s finality drawback manageable and enables repeated reanimation.
Permanent exile of one non-Salamander is strong but costs four and gives a 4/3 token; Larcenist is cheaper, flying and can affect multiple players' permanents temporarily.
Tapped three-color land replaced by a utility land that supports the core finality-counter engine; overall 34-land count and UBR fixing remain acceptable.
Mandatory combat-damage draw and 6/6 body are strong, but draw is already plentiful; Navigator is a Pirate and a high-ceiling extra-turn target for the commander.
Damage doubling can be lethal, but Ravager's ETB is immediate, can be doubled by Roaming Throne and can be reused through finality-counter mitigation.
